correctness.rationale: All constants follow from exact monomial angular moments and radial beta factors, with Gauss duplication and Euler transformation correctly producing the rational polynomial and denominator exponent. Pfaff maps it to \(P_m^{(d-\tfrac12,\pm\tfrac12)}\), with both Jacobi exponents above -1, implying m distinct roots on (-1,1) and exactly m simple negative scalar roots after the Cayley map. Real-rootedness makes Descartes sign variation equal the positive-root count of \(Q(u-1)\), including the \(u=0\) boundary case. Every \(|s|<1\) is realized by a ball inner product. Exact-rational independent series checks: 5776 coefficients plus examples. Finite tests alone are not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The special ball formula and all-negative simple scalar zero geometry with an exact rational zero count were not established in the inspected full-text primary works. Closest source Marinescu–Xing concerns real-analytic dependence of distance-weighted kernels, Beberok treats distinct ellipsoidal domains, and Zeytuncu/Perälä concern different radial disk problems. Direct unpublished-prior-claim deduplication separated the higher-dimensional assertion from a one-variable classification. Multiple targeted mathematical queries returned no dominating claim. This does not exclude unindexed equivalent work.
residual_risks: An unindexed work on exact radial-weighted Bergman kernels could already contain an equivalent formula or stronger result.

value.rationale: The Lu Qi-Keng zero problem for the natural Euclidean boundary-distance weight is resolved at every complex-ball dimension \(d\ge2\) and every integer \(t\ge0\): all zero levels are located on the negative axis and their exact number requires only rational arithmetic. The dimension-dependent transition from \(d=2,t=3\) (zero) to \(d=3,t=3\) (no zero), and back at \(d=3,t=4\) (zero), shows a nontrivial natural geometric feature absent from ordinary radial squared-distance weights. This is a natural complete classification, not an arbitrary finite slice; no larger downstream theorem is asserted.
